scope_note: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for TierPoint's Little Rock data center at 15707 Chenal Parkway in Pulaski County, Arkansas. Current operator and assessor records support two separately defined operating-floor-area observations; existing canonical assessor and Treasurer records retain parcel values and one unpaid tax-account amount. The selected building is kept separate from Windstream's 4001 Rodney Parham headquarters, its nationwide data-center portfolio, a nearby former trampoline/car-wash building that historically reused 15707 Chenal Parkway, and unrelated Acxiom facilities. Parcel sale prices, portfolio transaction values, headquarters incentives, a void right-of-way permit, equipment ratings, storage-tank registrations and a current vacancy are not relabeled as project investment, construction spending, resource use, employment or public contribution. Gap closure found no site-attributable capital outlay, construction workforce or payroll, supplier payment or local-purchase share, operating headcount or payroll, cash tax receipt or recipient distribution, realized incentive, marginal public-service cost, metered annual electricity, water or wastewater, emissions, or recipient-verified community contribution. No modeled synthesis is retained because none of the candidate estimates has complete, same-scope inputs or a defensible treatment design.

sources.title: Little Rock Data Center
sources.notes: The current operator page identifies Little Rock (LIT) at 15707 Chenal Parkway and reports 30,000+ total square feet, 9,000+ square feet of raised floor, two redundant 2.25 MW generators with at least 48 hours of runtime, 24x7x365 onsite security personnel and 24x7 remote-hands support. sources.title: Windstream Opens Little Rock Data Center
sources.notes: The predecessor's dated release announces the 30,000-square-foot Little Rock data center open on April 12, 2012, with a formal event scheduled for April 19. It describes 2N power, parallel UPS, redundant HVAC, 900 tons of cooling and an onsite network operations center staffed 24/7/365, but gives no address, project investment, construction spending, jobs, wages, payroll, supplier payments, incentives, taxes, public cost or resource consumption. The exact-address crosswalk comes from current operator, assessor and City records rather than from this release alone.

sources.title: Windstream Completes Sale of Data Center Assets to TierPoint
sources.notes: The release establishes the December 18, 2015 operator transition and a $575 million all-cash sale of Windstream's data-center business, plus transfer of former Hosted Solutions employees and customers. The transaction covers a nationwide business and publishes no Little Rock purchase-price, asset, employee or customer allocation. It is therefore chronology evidence only and is not treated as selected-project investment, payroll or local contribution.

sources.notes: Repository county economic panels derived from official BEA real-GDP and BLS QCEW employment and nominal average-weekly-wage series were reviewed for Pulaski County FIPS 05119 over 2001-2024. project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — address reuse and portfolio values kept separate
project_updates.notes: Direct pass and gap closure used the Windstream opening release, current TierPoint page/specification, TierPoint/SEC sale filings, IM3 coordinates, Pulaski assessor parcel 44L0750200100, deed numbers 2011-012158, 2014-040310, 2015-078938, 2016-069278 and 2023-035123, City zoning Z-4933-J, current adjacent-business address 15701, web archives and local reporting for 2003-2026. The evidence supports a February 2011 Windstream parcel purchase, an April 12, 2012 announced opening, December 2015 portfolio transfer to TierPoint and current operation. The 1993 building predates the data-center announcement; the $575 million portfolio transaction has no Little Rock allocation; assessor deed prices are property transfers, not cumulative project investment; and the former trampoline/car-wash building's historical reuse of 15707 is excluded without parcel/footprint crosswalk.
project_updates.project_description: TierPoint's Little Rock data center operates at 15707 Chenal Parkway in Little Rock, Pulaski County, Arkansas, in a 1993 building the assessor classifies as a 30,970-square-foot computer center. Windstream Hosted Solutions bought the parcel in February 2011 and announced the 30,000-square-foot center open on April 12, 2012; TierPoint took over the data-center business in December 2015 and the current parcel owner is TierPoint Properties LLC. Current operator specifications report 30,000+ total square feet, 9,000+ raised-floor space, and two 2.25 MW redundant generators, while state records separately register two 4,000-gallon diesel tanks at the site. Historic planning and business listings reused 15707 for an adjacent trampoline/car-wash property now numbered 15701, so address-only records are not assigned to this project without a parcel or facility crosswalk.

project_updates.notes: Pulaski County Assessor parcel detail, legal/land-use, property-record-card, sales and valuation-history views and the Treasurer mobile inquiry were searched by 44L0750200100, 44L-075.02-001.00, 15707 Chenal, TierPoint Properties, TierPoint Hosted Solutions, Windstream Hosted Solutions and One Source Addition for displayed 2004-2026 history. Existing canonical records retain 2011, 2012, 2017-2024 and 2026 assessed/taxable values, 2026 appraised value and the 2025 $82,440.85 Amount Due. Duplicate 2013 and 2025 valuation revisions remain unresolved; 2013-2016 annual gaps are not interpolated. The Treasurer's public mobile workflow and scripts expose current search/amount-due and checkout functions but no payment history or recipient distribution. No separate personal-property account, exemption, cash receipt or payment transaction was found; the unpaid amount due is not relabeled taxes paid or a recurring contribution, and a negative name search is not proof that no differently indexed account exists.

project_updates.title: Investment, construction, supplier and operating-model decisions — every candidate rejected
project_updates.notes: Investment candidate: converting 'multimillion-dollar,' the 2011 $2.697 million property purchase, 2014/2015 sale-leaseback prices or the $575 million portfolio sale into facility capital investment is rejected because the first is unbounded, deed prices are asset transfers and the portfolio price has no site allocation. Construction candidate: the rejected $5,000 right-of-way application cannot be summed or multiplied, and the opening-era retrofit lacks issued-permit value, audited outlay, asset mix, duration, workers, hours, payroll and local residence. Supplier/indirect candidate: applying an input-output multiplier or transferred local-purchase share is rejected because no eligible direct-spend base, paid vendor amount, multiplier vintage/geography or channel separation exists. Operations/household candidate: multiplying a current vacancy or 24/7 staffing language by its advertised wage band, interpolating corporate employment, or transferring county occupational wages is rejected because no facility headcount, annual-average FTE, occupation mix, payroll, residence or selected-building allocation exists. Leaving these metrics as gaps is more accurate and decision-useful than fabricated category totals.

project_updates.title: Fiscal, public-cost, resource and community-model decisions — no same-scope base survives
project_updates.notes: Fiscal candidate: aggregating or annualizing assessed values, deed prices, state RST fees or the 2025 $82,440.85 Amount Due is rejected because value stocks and fees are different metrics, the tax charge is not a cash receipt, recipient distributions are missing and personal property is unobserved. A public-service-cost break-even identity is also rejected: unlike a verified same-period contribution, an unpaid amount due cannot define a same-recipient revenue threshold, so no positive or negative net fiscal result is supportable. Incentive counterfactuals are rejected because the company-level entries and headquarters QACF payments have no selected-project agreement/allocation. Resource candidates that apply utilization factors to generator capacity, 48-hour backup duration or diesel-tank volume are rejected because the equipment is emergency backup and no load, runtime, deliveries, efficiency, meter or cooling inputs exist. Community annualization is rejected because no Little Rock recipient amount or complete giving ledger was found. No synthesis fragment is added.

project_updates.title: GDP, employment and wage outcome decisions — 2012 is not a clean county treatment
project_updates.notes: The governed BEA/BLS county panel for Pulaski County FIPS 05119 was reviewed over 2001-2024 with candidate pre-periods ending in 2011, a 2012 opening anchor and possible post-periods through 2024. GDP candidate: difference-in-differences, event-study and synthetic-control approaches are rejected because the selected building was already a 1993 computer center, Acxiom had another Little Rock data center by fiscal 2006, the treatment intensity is unknown and concurrent headquarters/sector shocks cannot be separated. Employment candidate: the same timing and donor failures apply, and neither the current vacancy nor corporate headcounts measure facility or county job contribution. Wage candidate: the same identification failures apply; no facility payroll or occupation mix exists and county nominal average weekly wages mix inflation and industry composition. A descriptive county gap is also rejected as insufficiently decision-relevant because it cannot distinguish this small retrofit/operation from the diverse county economy. No county comparison is presented as a project effect and no public-records requests or other solicitations were made.
